name: Neural Feedback Carbine NFC-3 'Mirrorgun'
description:
The NFC-3 does not fire a conventional projectile. It emits a tightly focused stream of encoded neural feedback signals derived from the operator's own nervous system, sampled in real time through a sensor array embedded in the grip and stock. The signal stream is amplified, phase-inverted, and projected at the target via a coherent electromagnetic emitter in the barrel. When the stream contacts a target with active neural augmentation — cybernetic nervous system components, neural interface implants, or synaptic enhancement hardware — it creates a feedback loop between the target's augmentation and the projected signal, producing effects ranging from temporary motor disruption to complete neurological shutdown depending on the intensity setting and the target's augmentation profile.

Ringo Corponation developed the NFC-3 as a counter-augmentation platform, responding to the tactical problem of heavily cyberware-augmented combatants who could shrug off conventional firearms due to pain suppression systems and reflex enhancements. The feedback loop exploits the fundamental architecture of neural augmentation: the more extensively a target is augmented, the more vulnerable they are to a correctly tuned feedback stream. Against fully unaugmented targets, the NFC-3 is almost entirely ineffective — the emitted signal has no neural hardware to interact with and dissipates without meaningful effect. This limitation is the weapon's defining tactical characteristic.

The grip sensor array must maintain contact with the operator's bare skin to sample the neural signal baseline. Operators wearing full gloves cannot use the weapon effectively — a deliberate design choice that Ringo Corponation defends as a safety feature preventing unauthorized use, though critics note it also makes the weapon impractical in environments requiring full protective equipment. The weapon's emitter produces a faint violet luminescence during discharge that is invisible to standard optics but detectable to augmented visual systems — a cruel irony given the weapon's primary target demographic.
legality: Prohibited (counter-augmentation weapons treaty violations in 7 jurisdictions)
specifications:
emission type: Encoded neural feedback signal stream
effective range: 30m (full effect) / 50m (partial effect)
intensity settings: 5 stages — Motor disruption / Sensory overload / Coordination failure / Augmentation lockout / Neurological shutdown
rate of fire: Continuous beam (sustained) / Pulse mode
weight: 2.8 kg
power source: High-density capacitor bank, 40 seconds sustained fire per charge
operator requirement: Bare-skin grip contact for neural signal sampling
effectiveness against unaugmented: Negligible
visual signature: Violet luminescence (invisible to standard optics, visible to augmented vision)
tactical_use: Deployed specifically against augmented targets in environments where conventional firearms are ineffective due to the target's pain suppression and reflex systems. Standard doctrine is to sweep the beam across the target rather than hold a fixed point, as movement disrupts the feedback loop coherence and reduces effectiveness. In team operations, the NFC-3 operator is typically shielded by conventional firearms users who handle unaugmented threats while the Mirrorgun operator concentrates on augmented targets. The weapon is considered a specialist tool requiring significant operator training to use effectively.
cultural_context: The Mirrorgun occupies a uniquely contentious space in GLMZ's cultural landscape around augmentation. For augmented individuals — a significant and politically vocal population — it represents one of the most direct expressions of fear and hostility toward their existence: a weapon designed specifically to hurt people because they have implants. Anti-augmentation political factions have quietly funded Ringo Corponation's development program, while augmentation rights advocates have made the NFC-3 a centerpiece of their arguments that augmented individuals face systematic persecution. In street culture, being targeted with a Mirrorgun is considered a profound insult regardless of whether it causes injury.
known_users: Government security forces in jurisdictions with active augmentation restrictions
story_hooks: An augmented street medic who treated victims of NFC-3 attacks is now a target herself — someone is using a Mirrorgun to silence witnesses to a corporate operation. She needs protection and the players need to trace the weapon back to whoever authorized its use, which means following a supply chain that Ringo Corponation has deliberately obscured.

A stolen NFC-3 is being used by someone who doesn't understand its limitations — they're firing it at unaugmented targets and getting no results, then escalating to conventional violence in frustration. The players are hired to recover the weapon before its erratic user kills someone, but the recovery means going into territory controlled by an anti-augmentation faction that will not welcome outsiders.

Ringo Corponation approaches the players to field-test a new NFC-3 firmware update that claims to extend effectiveness against partially augmented targets. The test parameters are suspiciously specific, and the 'test subjects' Ringo has identified are activists who have been publicly critical of the weapon's development. The players have to decide whether to run the test, expose Ringo's intentions, or find a third option.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular carbine with an almost surgical precision to its design. The barrel is noticeably slender and tapers slightly, housing the electromagnetic emitter array. The profile suggests a weapon built for neural precision rather than kinetic force — less brutalist assault rifle, more specialized medical instrument. The stock and grip are ergonomically sculpted with visible sensor arrays breaking the surface.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94 cm | Barrel length: 38 cm | Stock depth: 22 cm | Grip width: 4.2 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light and well-balanced at 2.8 kg — floats naturally in the firing position. The weight distribution pulls slightly toward the barrel despite the compact form, hinting at the heavy capacitor bank housed deeper in the body. Feels almost delicate compared to conventional carbines of similar length.
physical_description.primary_material: Primary frame: Carbon-composite skeletal structure with titanium-alloy reinforcement at stress points. Barrel housing: Brushed steel electromagnetic containment sleeve. Grip section: Textured polymer with embedded sensor nodules.
physical_description.finish: Matte black primary finish with brushed steel accents. The barrel housing catches light differently — intentionally high-polish to manage thermal dissipation from the emitter array. Sensor array contact points on grip show slight wear patterns from repeated bare-skin contact, creating micro-scratches in the finish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Deep matte black | Accents: Brushed steel gray | Highlights: Thin violet accent lines running along the barrel shroud (dormant state) | Sensor node contacts: gunmetal gray
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with deliberate micro-texturing designed to maximize bare-skin contact. Slightly tacky to touch — engineered to prevent slipping when wet with sweat or blood. The texture transitions to smoother titanium-reinforced sections at trigger guard and charging mechanism.
distinctive_features: Visible sensor array embedded in grip — small circular contact nodes (8-12mm diameter) arranged in a grid pattern across palm and fingers contact zones
Coherent electromagnetic emitter array visible as a series of stacked ring-shaped components within the clear polymer-windowed barrel shroud

Five-position intensity dial on the left side of the receiver — marked with stylized icons rather than numbers (motor disruption symbol → sensory overload → coordination failure → augmentation lockout → shutdown symbol)
Pulse/Continuous toggle switch disguised as minimal aggressive geometry in the safety area
High-density capacitor pack visible through right-side reinforced viewport — cylindrical ceramic component with cooling fins
Thermal vent array along the length of the barrel shroud designed to bleed off electromagnetic field heat
Zero conventional iron sights — mounting rails absent; weapon is designed entirely for integrated augmented targeting systems or direct aim
Emitter discharge port: unusual octagonal geometry rather than circular — designed to shape the neural feedback beam profile
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: RINGO CORPONATION logo embossed in recessed rectangle on the left side of the receiver, just forward of the intensity dial. Serial plate mounted on the underside of the barrel shroud — stainless steel with laser-etched alphanumeric code. Small text warning printed in three languages along the grip: 'BARE SKIN CONTACT REQUIRED | INEFFECTIVE AGAINST UNAUGMENTED TARGETS | CLASS-A BIOHAZARD EMISSION'
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually encountered in one of two states: either pristine and carefully maintained by military quartermasters (specialist tools receive obsessive care), or showing signs of heavy field use with scorched polymer patches, micro-fractures in the barrel shroud viewport, and polished contact points on the grip from repeated neural sampling. Battle-scarred examples show discoloration around the vent array from repeated electromagnetic discharge cycling.
